item.text: {"text":"Recent work challenges the assumption that better random-negative separation guarantees better top-ten ranking. [Scaled cross-entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14238) analyzes CE’s ranking coverage and tightness: full-softmax CE offers advantages over pointwise/pairwise objectives, but remains an imperfect surrogate for ranking metrics; scaling the sampled normalization term is proposed when full softmax is impractical. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721), approximates CE using maximum-inner-product selection of informative competing items. Neither establishes an HR@10-specific optimum. A [2024 sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent trade-offs: uniform negatives favor popular items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance while lowering aggregate accuracy.\n\nHardness also risks suppressing plausible positives. [NARec (2025)](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1049/aie2.70004) combines batch/global negative selection with dynamically generated hard negatives. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) explicitly identifies potential false negatives and uses teacher soft labels, supporting caution about treating every high-scoring unobserved item as irrelevant; its teacher mechanism should not be copied under this task’s single-model constraint. A task-compatible hypothesis is one BERT4Rec per category, comparing masked-target full CE against sampled CE with mixed uniform and model-mined negatives, excluding known training positives and limiting aggressive hard-negative weighting. Preserve appended-MASK inference and treat false-negative filtering as an ablation, not established truth. No reviewed evidence establishes gains specifically on Electronics or Industrial_and_Scientific under this evaluator; select solely by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10."}
